sections.h2: Who assesses, bills and collects property tax in Letcher County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Three offices split the work in Letcher County. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) values each parcel, the Letcher County Sheriff mails and collects the current-year bill, and the Letcher County Clerk takes over bills that go unpaid past April 15.

The PVA works from 156 Main Street, Suite 105, in Whitesburg (office 606-633-2182, fax 606-633-3995) and keeps weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Its county page notes that the assessment date and the owner of record are both fixed as of January 1. Anyone who buys after that date will see the bill in the former owner's name until the next calendar year, so a new owner who never receives a copy should call the sheriff at 606-633-2293.

The county's own website lists the sheriff's department with the same number and weekday hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and it links to an online payment page for property tax. The Letcher County Clerk is reachable at 606-633-2432 on the same weekday schedule, and its site carries a delinquent tax section. Ask the clerk's office for the date of the current year's tax sale.

sections.h2: What is Letcher County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Letcher County sits in the far southeast corner of Kentucky, and its terrain does most of the explaining. Pine Mountain runs 125 miles and splits the county, Black Mountain forms the Virginia line at about 3,700 feet, and Jefferson National Forest covers a large share of the land. The county was cut from parts of Harlan, Perry and Pike in 1842 and named for a governor of that era. Whitesburg is the county seat and Jenkins the largest city, with Fleming-Neon as the third city and Blackey, Mayking, McRoberts, Millstone and Payne Gap as census-designated places.

Coal built the modern county. The population had never passed 10,000 before mining arrived, then climbed past 40,000 by 1940, and the county produced more than 600 million short tons of coal between 1990 and 2014. The Census Bureau now estimates 19,952 residents for July 2025, a drop of 7.4 percent from the 2020 base. A thin buyer pool and long distances shape pricing here more than any tax rule.

Two school systems serve the county. Letcher County Public Schools covers most addresses, including the high school in Whitesburg, while Jenkins Independent Schools serves the Jenkins area from a combined middle and high school and an elementary school in Burdine. US 23 crosses the eastern edge, US 119 links Jenkins to Whitesburg over Pine Mountain, and Kentucky 15 runs northwest toward Knott County. The July and August 2022 flooding across eastern Kentucky took three lives in this county and left many people without homes, so a seller with a damaged building should ask the PVA how the damage is reflected in the assessment.

sections.h2: When is Letcher County property tax due, and what do late bills cost?
sections.html:
The bill is due by December 31 of the assessment year, and Kentucky's collection statute (KRS 134.015) sets a ladder of discounts and penalties that the Letcher County Sheriff applies. If the county's bills are delayed, the Department of Revenue can substitute an alternative schedule that gives owners one month at each stage.

  • Paid in full by November 1: 2 percent off the bill.
  • November 2 through December 31: the face amount, with no discount or penalty.
  • January 1 through January 31: a 5 percent penalty.
  • After January 31: a 10 percent penalty, with the sheriff's add-on fee on top.
  • After close of business on April 15: unpaid bills move to the Letcher County Clerk as certificates of delinquency and a lien is recorded.

At the clerk's office, interest runs at 1 percent a month, and the clerk and county attorney charge commissions that grow with each notice. The state's worked example turns a $1,000 bill into $1,254 when it reaches the clerk, and into $1,659.90 if it is still unpaid after the June advertisement. A third-party purchaser may then buy the debt at a tax sale held between 90 and 135 days after the transfer, and the lien stays attached for eleven years whoever owns the house.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Letcher County assessment?
sections.html:
Meet with the PVA before anything else. State law requires a conference with the PVA or a deputy before an appeal can be filed, and the conference has to happen before or during the inspection period.

The tax roll is open to public inspection for 13 days starting on the first Monday of May each year. An owner who held a conference has until the close of business on the day after inspection ends to file the appeal with the Letcher County Clerk. The local board of assessment appeals then convenes at the county seat, Whitesburg, no sooner than 25 and no later than 35 days after inspection closes.

  • Bring physical details of the land and buildings, insurance policies, construction costs and real estate listings. A board must deny an appeal that arrives without this kind of evidence.
  • A paid representative must be an attorney, accountant, tax consultant, Kentucky real estate broker or sales associate, licensed appraiser, an employee of the owner or hold a recognized appraisal designation, and must present written authorization.
  • Owners may record the hearing on audio, and the board must explain in writing any change it makes.
  • If bills go out before the appeal ends, a higher final value produces a supplemental bill.

sections.h2: Does Letcher County offer a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Yes. For the 2025 and 2026 assessment years the exemption removes $49,100 from the assessed value of a qualifying home, so a house assessed at $120,000 would be taxed on $70,900.

The owner must be 65 or older during the year, or be classified as totally disabled under a federal program or a retirement system, and must own and live in the house. With 21.9 percent of county residents past 65, this is a common situation. File the application with the Letcher County PVA. Owners under 65 with a disability usually reapply each year, though veterans with a service-connected disability and people found permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems document the disability once. The exemption follows the owner and not the house, so a buyer must apply in their own name.

sections.h2: What happens to Letcher County property tax when I sell?
sections.html:
The bill follows whoever owned the parcel on January 1, and the closing statement decides who pays what. In many Kentucky sales the seller credits the buyer for the months the seller owned the house, and the buyer then pays the full bill when it arrives. Check the settlement statement line by line.

The Kentucky real estate transfer tax under KRS 142.050 is 50 cents for each $500 of value, charged to the seller named in the deed and collected by the county clerk when the deed is recorded. Transfers made through foreclosure, between spouses in a divorce, or between parent and child for nominal consideration are exempt. Unpaid property tax does not disappear at closing: it is a lien that survives the sale, so title work normally clears it from the proceeds. Ask the Letcher County Sheriff for a payoff figure before the closing date, and ask the clerk whether any certificate of delinquency has been recorded against the parcel.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to in Letcher County?
faqs.a: Pay the Letcher County Sheriff. The sheriff's department can be reached at 606-633-2293 on weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and the county website links to an online payment page. Bills left unpaid after April 15 move to the county clerk.

faqs.q: Can I get a discount on a Letcher County tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes, 2 percent comes off when the bill is paid in full by November 1 of the assessment year. After that the face amount applies through December 31, then a 5 percent penalty in January and 10 percent after January 31.

faqs.q: What if I never received a tax bill after buying in Letcher County?
faqs.a: Call the sheriff at 606-633-2293 and ask for a copy. Bills are issued in the name of the owner of record on January 1, so a recent buyer's bill may carry the previous owner's name, and an unreceived bill does not excuse payment.

faqs.q: Where do I file a property tax appeal in Letcher County?
faqs.a: File it with the Letcher County Clerk after meeting with the PVA at 156 Main Street, Suite 105 in Whitesburg. The deadline is one workday after the 13-day tax roll inspection period ends, which starts on the first Monday in May.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller owe Letcher County tax at closing?
faqs.a: The closing statement settles it. The sheriff's bill goes to the January 1 owner, and Kentucky sellers commonly credit the buyer for the part of the year they held the house. Any delinquent amount is a lien that must be paid for the title to pass clean.
